verdicts.note: Refers to herself as a girl/woman engineer throughout; female confirmed.
Explicitly states she does chemical engineering.
Says her schooling was 'a mixed co-ed school'; Mixed sex correct.
'I start the second year after my first year' supports Part B/Year 2.
'I thought it would be interesting' supports agree.
'it's challenging so I think I like' supports agree.
Quote says the DEGREE is maths-based (an attraction), not that she was good at maths/science at school; construct not supported.
'very wide industry – very broad' is a neutral 5-word description of the industry, not a statement that variety appealed to her in choosing to study.
'I didn't know 100% what engineering's all about until I did it myself' supports little prior knowledge.
Father is an engineer and 'introduced this engineering thing'; siblings/friends in engineering = how she knew of it. Strong support.
Father 'introduced' engineering (and 'didn't really tell me what he's doing'); introduction is weaker than active encouragement — agree defensible but thin, downgrade.
'No one really discourage me' supports no.
Cited quote (tutor/parents) is about placement, not studying engineering; father 'introduced' engineering weakly supports disagree, but evidence is off-target — downgrade.
Flat 'Yes' to pleased plus 'More than what I expected'; supports positive but 'Strongly agree' is at the upper edge — downgrade confidence.
Course develops leadership/team-working/communication skills — supports interpersonal-skills development.
'I like it very much that I learn a lot from it' supports satisfied.
Design coursework named the best thing about the course — supports very satisfied.
'my personal tutor is fine' is modest but positive — satisfied defensible, medium confidence appropriate.
Came to this university to go for a placement; placement arranged — yes.
'Firstly, you expect to get the experience' names it as primary reason; supports strong, but downgrade slightly as a single ranking cue.
Looks forward to working in a 'proper big British company' — supports wanting to see what industry is like.

Subject quote is about real/first-hand experience vs 'a piece of paper'; theory-application framing partly seeded by interviewer ('put things you've learnt into practice') — adjacent, thin, downgrade.
'learn how to deal with things but in more mature way' supports personal development.
'doing research in chemical engineering' supports research/development, though in tension with process-engineer/site ideal; medium appropriate.
'working as a process engineer' plus on-site/doing-the-work ideal supports technical/specialist.
'still thinking of doing research in chemical engineering' supports intention for further study.
Research in chemical engineering = engineering related subject.
